Synopsis:
    Indian corporates (PFC, REC, Bajaj Finance, Cholamandalam) are pivoting to long-duration debt issuance (10–15yr+), raising ₹120bn in four days, driven by structural demand from insurers and pension funds needing liability matching. The shift is partly tactical: hawkish RBI commentary has pushed up short-end corporate yields, compressing the relative appeal of near-term borrowing. Reduced supply of long-dated sovereign paper (GOI cut ultra-long share from 35% to 25%) and lighter state issuance are amplifying demand for long-dated corporate bonds. Some market participants caution the trend is not a structural shift but rather opportunistic absorption by specific investor classes.
